name: Conformal risk control for railway signal detection (SNCF dataset)
org: IRT Saint Exupery / ANITI / SNCF (DEEL program)
modality: Object detector (YOLOv5m, DETR-ResNet50, DiffusionDet) fed train-operator-view RGB frames (1280x720); scored by empirical coverage / risk of conformalised bounding boxes at alpha=0.1 and by 'stretch' (box inflation needed to reach the guarantee)
what_it_measures: Whether split conformal prediction and conformal risk control give formally guaranteed miscoverage (<=10%) on detected railway signals, and the price in box size. Positioned as a first step toward certifiable perception for trains.
size: 41 railway-line videos, 3414 images, 3508 boxes; splits 1914 cal / 1500 test (pretrained) or 1414 fit / 1000 cal / 1000 test (fine-tuned)
reported_metrics: Target alpha=0.1; empirical coverage reported close to 0.9 for additive box-wise CP; Hausdorff-style conformalisation gives unusable (huge) boxes; image-wise CRC sometimes unattainable for weak detectors
cost_evidence: Manual annotation of all signals on ~3.4k frames extracted from ~1.5 h videos; fine-tuning 100 epochs YOLOv5m; no wall-clock or dollar cost stated
validity_evidence: Finite-sample coverage guarantee is distribution-free by construction; no field validation or link to operational incident rates
notes: Closest thing in Fel's record to a safety evaluation of an autonomous-system component. Fel is second author; Andeol led. Short companion paper: 'Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy Detection of Railway Signals', AI and Ethics 4:157-161 (2024), arXiv:2301.11136 (fetched, same authors, same dataset). Not a robot; a perception module for a train.

name: Human-centered utility benchmark for attribution methods (Meta-predictor)
modality: Image classifier + attribution heatmaps shown to crowdworkers; scored by 'Utility' = AUC of how much explanations improve humans' ability to predict the model's decisions vs no-explanation baseline
what_it_measures: Whether explanation methods actually help humans understand a model in three scenarios (bias detection, expert strategy, failure cases), and whether standard faithfulness metrics (Deletion) predict that usefulness.
size: n=1150 AMT participants (240-242 retained per scenario after screening), 6 attribution methods, 3 datasets (Husky vs Wolf, Leaves, ImageNet)
reported_metrics: Grad-CAM (p<0.001), Occlusion (p=0.01), SmoothGrad (p=0.034) significantly useful for bias detection; no method useful on ImageNet; faithfulness (1-Deletion) shows no positive correlation with human utility, if anything anti-correlated; strong correlation with perceptual similarity and explanation complexity
cost_evidence: 1150 paid crowdworkers via Amazon Mechanical Turk; ~30 subjects per condition
validity_evidence: Direct human-in-the-loop measurement; key finding is that proxy metrics do NOT predict human-measured value
notes: Not embodied. Directly relevant to a value-of-information argument: shows cheap proxy metrics can have zero or negative information about the quantity that matters. Venue NeurIPS 2022 from memory of proceedings; arXiv v3 Jan 2023.

name: MeGe / ReCo stability measures for explanation quality
org: ANITI Toulouse / IRT Saint Exupery / Brown
modality: Image classifiers (standard vs 1-Lipschitz); explanations scored by mean generalizability (MeGe) and relative consistency (ReCo), metrics borrowed from algorithmic stability
what_it_measures: Whether explanations are stable across retrainings on data subsets; argues fidelity metrics alone are insufficient for trustworthy explanations.
size: Multiple architectures, methods and datasets (counts not in abstract)
reported_metrics: 1-Lipschitz networks obtain higher MeGe and ReCo than standard networks at similar accuracy
cost_evidence: Requires training several models on data folds; none stated numerically
notes: Earlier title 'Representativity and Consistency Measures for Deep Neural Network Explanations' (2020 preprint). Interpretability-metric work, not robot safety.

name: Xplique explainability toolbox (methods + evaluation metrics)
org: DEEL / IRT Saint Exupery / ANITI / Brown
modality: Any TF/PyTorch vision or tabular model; ships 26 attribution methods and 15 explanation-evaluation metrics (fidelity: Deletion, Insertion, MuFidelity; stability; MeGe/ReCo; randomization checks)
what_it_measures: Provides a standard implementation for benchmarking explanation methods; developed inside the DEEL certifiable-AI program (aerospace/rail partners).
notes: Coauthors include SNCF (Nicodeme, Gardes) and IRT (Flandin) staff; the DEEL context is certification of ML in critical systems, but the paper itself has no robot or vehicle evaluation. GitHub https://github.com/deel-ai/xplique fetched.

name: Baseline effects on explainability fidelity metrics
modality: Image classifiers; Insertion/Deletion fidelity metrics computed under different perturbation baselines; ranks of attribution methods compared across baselines
what_it_measures: Shows that the ranking of attribution methods under standard fidelity metrics flips with the choice of baseline, even for linear models; proposes a model-dependent baseline via feature visualisation.
reported_metrics: Qualitative: different baselines favour different methods; trade-off between information removal and out-of-distribution inputs
validity_evidence: none stated (paper is about the metric's own validity)
notes: Meta-evaluation of an evaluation metric; relevant as evidence that benchmark design choices can dominate outcomes. Not embodied.

name: Unified concept-extraction framework with new evaluation metrics (Lens)
modality: ImageNet classifiers; concept dictionaries scored by new metrics for concept extraction and importance estimation; 'strategic cluster graph' visualisation
what_it_measures: Frames concept-based explainability as dictionary learning and introduces evaluation metrics for concept extraction and importance methods, with optimality guarantees.
size: All 1000 ImageNet classes visualised in the Lens resource
notes: Core interpretability paper; included only because it defines evaluation metrics. No safety or embodied content.

name: Archetypal SAE with plausibility and identifiability benchmarks
modality: Large vision models (e.g. DINOv2); SAE dictionaries scored on (i) plausibility: recovery of true classification directions, (ii) identifiability: separation of synthetic concept mixtures with known ground truth
what_it_measures: Stability and correctness of concept dictionaries extracted by sparse autoencoders; introduces two benchmarks with known ground truth.
reported_metrics: RA-SAE outperforms standard SAEs on both benchmarks while matching reconstruction (numbers in paper, not abstract)
validity_evidence: Synthetic ground truth for identifiability; no downstream safety validation
notes: Likely the closest to Fel's SPAIS talk content (SAEs for vision). Benchmark is for interpretability tools, not for robots.

name: Controlled evaluation of SAE architectures (MP-SAE)
modality: Synthetic and MNIST settings with known correlated/hierarchical features; SAE variants scored on feature recovery and reconstruction
what_it_measures: Whether shallow SAE designs can recover correlated features; shows quasi-orthogonality assumption fails and proposes Matching-Pursuit SAE.
reported_metrics: MP-SAE gives monotonic reconstruction improvement with more atoms; recovers correlated features shallow SAEs miss

name: Psychophysical comparison of neuron vs dictionary bases
modality: ResNet50 and VGG16 units or dictionary atoms; humans judge visual coherence of maximally activating image sets; scored by human agreement
what_it_measures: Which representational basis yields explanations humans find coherent; dictionary-based bases win, especially in deep layers, and expose model differences neurons hide.
reported_metrics: Dictionary-based representations consistently rated more interpretable than neurons (effect sizes in paper)
validity_evidence: Human ratings are the target quantity; no downstream task validation
notes: Human-labelling cost example for evaluating interpretability tools.

name: Internal-representation monitors for reward hacking during evaluations
modality: Open-weight LLM agents (Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Qwen 3.8 Max) on coding evals (DeepSWE, SWE-bench); difference-of-means activation vectors used as a monitor; scored by hack detection rate at matched false-positive rate
what_it_measures: Whether reward hacking has a linear signature in activations that can be used as a runtime monitor during evaluations and to discover new hack types.
size: 2 benchmarks, 3 models; rollout counts in paper
reported_metrics: GLM 5.2 hacks in 57.2% of DeepSWE rollouts and 73% on SWE-bench; DoM monitors catch +3.1% more hacks (Kimi K3) and 7.9% fewer (GLM 5.2) than baseline at matched FPR
cost_evidence: Requires white-box activation access and rollouts on agentic benchmarks; no dollar cost stated
validity_evidence: Compared against labelled hacking rollouts; LLM domain only
notes: Fel is 15th of 18 authors. Only Fel-linked paper that is explicitly about safety monitoring during evaluations; not embodied. Goodfire blog post exists ('Models know when they're reward hacking', 17 Sept 2026) but its URL was not resolved.

name: Physics Emergence Zone in video world models
modality: Encoder-based video transformers; layerwise probes, subspace geometry, patch decoding and attention ablations on intuitive-physics benchmarks; scored by probe accuracy for speed, acceleration, direction
what_it_measures: Where and how physical variables become linearly accessible inside video encoders (a sharp intermediate-depth transition); direction is encoded on a circular manifold.
notes: Most embodied-adjacent Fel paper (world models for physical prediction). Interpretability probe study, not a safety evaluation.

name: The Case for Model Science (Verify, Explore, Steer, Refine)
org: Warsaw Univ. of Tech / TU Dublin / UTS / Harvard-Goodfire / Fraunhofer HHI
what_it_measures: Argues benchmarking is insufficient and proposes a discipline of per-model analysis organised as Verify / Explore / Steer / Refine, with shared catalogues of datasets, models and findings.
notes: Useful as a citable stance on the limits of benchmark-only evaluation; no robotics.

name: Conceptual blindspot audit of generative image models via SAEs
modality: Text-to-image models (SD 1.5/2.1, PixArt, Kandinsky); 32k-concept archetypal SAE on DINOv2 features compares concept prevalence in real vs generated images
what_it_measures: Systematic audit of which training-data concepts a generative model under- or over-produces, plus memorisation artefacts at the datapoint level.
reported_metrics: Qualitative blindspots (bird feeders, DVD discs suppressed; wood textures, palm trees exaggerated)
cost_evidence: Training a 32k-atom SAE on DINOv2 features; none stated numerically
notes: An interpretability-driven audit protocol; template for how SAE tooling could audit robot perception models, but no embodied content.
